tweets.text:
Is AI about to run into a debt problem?

Elon just confirmed something that’s becoming increasingly clear:

Companies without strong, consistent revenue are finding it harder to rely on debt financing.

Here are a few names that could be more exposed:

$CRWV: $35.6B in debt vs. $5.5B in cash. Its bonds are yielding around 15%.

$ORCL: $23.7B in negative free cash flow.

$CIFR: $6B in debt vs. just $832M in cash.

$APLD: $36.2B in contracts, but only $451M is expected to come in during FY27.

$IREN: $7.6B in debt vs. $5.9B in cash.

$NBIS: $8.5B in debt vs. $8B in cash, but the company is still unprofitable.

If borrowing becomes more expensive, companies with real revenue and strong cash flow should be in the best position to weather it.

The bigger question is simple:

What happens if investors stop funding AI growth with cheap debt?

quote.text:
Pretty much. 

As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. 

SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we’re investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.

That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many.

$BTC Big week(s).

Either Bitcoin holds $80K throughout these next 1-2 weeks with: FOMC, Earnings, Election(s), IPO filing(s), End/Start of the month flows & whatever geopolitical headlines we're going to see.

In that case I think we go to $87K and take out those equal highs there and target $90K+.

If price does lose $80K we'll find ourselves in a solid high timeframe value area (I think) in the mid to low $70Ks. Might chop around there for a while and things will look scary.
